request.description: Candidate-independent characterization of the loaded two-joint MuJoCo model: finite-grid constrained IK branch margins, compiled inertial and actuator quantities, and short zero/saturated control responses at representative configurations.
request.rationale: No learned candidate exists, so policy evaluation cannot yet distinguish exposure/branch geometry failures from transient control or physical-authority limits. request.current_synthesis: Observed in completed operation M1: the Runner executed the candidate-independent loaded-physics probe and produced a verified artifact. The loaded model has the expected two joints, 0.002 s physics timestep, zero gravity, 0.02 s official control interval, +/-1 controls, and gear 5. Compiled body masses and inertia are generated rather than specified in the XML; representative mass matrices vary with configuration, including shoulder diagonal values 0.01210, 0.01147 and 0.01093 kg*m^2 and shoulder-elbow coupling from 0.000507 to -0.000080 kg*m^2. Ten-substep constant saturated commands produced approximately 200–212 rad/s^2 joint accelerations and endpoint speeds from 0.61 to 1.64 m/s across the three configurations, whereas zero commands remained stationary. These observations establish that the loaded plant has meaningful, configuration-dependent transient authority and that momentum can be large over one official 20 ms interval; they do not establish policy failure, hold instability under feedback, or an unavoidable actuator limit because no policy episode was measured. The finite 15-by-25 radius-angle grid over both IK branches contained 708 feasible and 42 infeasible branch configurations. The infeasible records are branch-specific and symmetric across angle/branch; inspected examples show the alternate branch can be feasible for the same target (at r=0.06 m, angle -120 degrees, elbow-up is outside the shoulder range while elbow-down is feasible). The grid's worst feasible branch has only 0.751 degrees minimum joint-limit margin at r=0.12 m, angle -120 degrees, elbow-up. Thus the measurement supports branch-aware geometry as a consequential risk, but does not prove any official target is unreachable and explicitly is not a continuous reachability proof. Interpretation remains provisional: the physical model's competing explanations—branch/limit-conditioned acquisition versus transient overshoot/hold instability—both remain live, with dynamics authority now measured rather than assumed.
request.decision_frontier: The unresolved decision is which mechanism should determine the first learning direction: (A) branch/limit-conditioned target coverage and configuration acquisition, or (B) visible-state velocity-aware braking and stabilization for the 100-sample uninterrupted hold. M1 shows both can matter but is candidate-independent and short-horizon. Discriminating evidence is a complete candidate evaluation on the official target distribution with per-episode first-entry time, minimum/final distance, maximum held steps, hold interruptions, terminal reason, target radius/angle, inferred branch residuals and joint-limit margin, plus control saturation and velocity traces; substep traces should be added if boundary-level success/failure is not explained. A concentration of failures in low-margin angles/radii would redirect toward branch-aware exposure/control; broad failures with entry followed by exits or high arrival velocity would redirect toward stabilization. The finite grid's 42 branch violations must not be promoted to task infeasibility without target-level aggregation or observed episode failures.

pi_checkpoint.current_goal_gap: The best-known frozen candidate T1:checkpoint-115712 achieved 105/160 = 65.625% on the non-protected official-distribution development panel M2, far below the 196/200 requirement. It has no official assessment result. The dominant observed failure class for this recipe is no tolerance entry, but the campaign remains 91 successes short of the development-panel 98% equivalent and has not tested the full-band exposure candidate.
pi_checkpoint.current_synthesis: M1 established candidate-independent physical priors: the loaded arm has configuration-dependent compiled inertia and transient authority, one 20 ms interval can carry substantial momentum, and finite-grid IK feasibility and joint-limit margins vary by branch; it did not establish an actuator ceiling or policy failure. T1 trained the unchanged PPO recipe (tanh 64x64, current reward, 11-value runtime, 14–20 cm exposure) for 120,000 requested steps and completed 120,832; its late proxy success near 0.96 only nominates a checkpoint within that restricted exposure and is not development performance. M2 evaluated the frozen pre-terminal plateau checkpoint T1:checkpoint-115712 on 160 official-distribution development episodes and measured 105 successes (65.625%). All 55 failures truncated at the horizon; 49 had maximum held steps zero and never entered tolerance, while 6 entered at steps 14–25 and later interrupted with nonzero measured velocities. The no-entry failures skewed inward, supporting missing inward exposure as a credible hypothesis, but M2 also found failures at larger radii and varied joint-limit margins, so it does not establish exposure as the cause or separate exposure from branch/limit-conditioned acquisition. The inherited statement that exposure/branch-conditioned acquisition dominates should therefore be narrowed: M2 establishes a recipe-specific no-entry failure predominance, not a causal exposure conclusion. The minority post-entry interruptions keep transient stabilization consequential, but they are not the first bottleneck for this tested artifact. E7 opens I2 to test the complete full-band candidate with fixed reward, observation/runtime, robot, timing, and success semantics; any causal claim will remain limited to the compared artifacts and recorded implementation.
pi_checkpoint.decision_frontier: The unresolved consequential distinction is whether the 14–20 cm exposure gap is sufficient to explain a material part of the official failure gap, or whether inward targets expose branch/limit-conditioned acquisition failures that require a different control or representation direction. The discriminating comparison is a fresh full-band-trained frozen artifact versus T1, evaluated on an official-distribution development panel with complete success, no-entry versus post-entry outcomes, target radius and angle, selected IK branch, minimum joint-limit margin, action saturation, and entry/hold velocity diagnostics. Improvement concentrated in 0.06–0.14 m with fewer no-entry failures supports retaining the full-band direction; persistent failures at healthy-margin or outer targets redirect toward branch-aware acquisition/control; remaining entry-then-interruption cases preserve velocity-aware stabilization as the next possible direction. Substep traces remain nonessential unless boundary-level diagnostics cannot explain hold exits; their current absence is an unresolved measurement limit, not evidence of hidden excursions.
pi_checkpoint.human_goal_connection: Advance toward a learned policy that achieves at least 98% episode success, meaning a complete uninterrupted 100-control-step hold, over the official full-angle 6–20 cm target distribution.
